passages.text: Then the fifth angel sounded his trumpet, and I saw a star that had fallen from heaven to earth, and it was given the key to the pit of the Abyss.
passages.sermon:
The fifth angel sounded his trumpet.
I saw a star.
This star had fallen from heaven to earth.
Someone gave the star a key.
This key opened the pit of the Abyss.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ πέμπτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν καὶ εἶδον ἀστέρα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πεπτωκότα εἰς τὴν γῆν καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἡ κλεὶς τοῦ φρέατος τῆς ἀβύσσου

passages.text: The star opened the pit of the Abyss, and smoke rose out of it like the smoke of a great furnace, and the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke from the pit.
passages.sermon:
A star had fallen from heaven to earth.
This star received the key to the pit of the Abyss.
The star opened the pit of the Abyss.
Smoke came out from the pit.
The smoke was like the smoke from a great furnace.
The smoke from the pit darkened the sun.
The smoke from the pit darkened the air.
passages.original: καὶ ἤνοιξεν τὸ φρέαρ τῆς ἀβύσσου καὶ ἀνέβη καπνὸς ἐκ τοῦ φρέατος ὡς καπνὸς καμίνου μεγάλης καὶ ἐσκοτώθη ὁ ἥλιος καὶ ὁ ἀὴρ ἐκ τοῦ καπνοῦ τοῦ φρέατος

passages.text: And out of the smoke, locusts descended on the earth, and they were given power like that of the scorpions of the earth.
passages.sermon:
Smoke rose from the pit of the Abyss.
Locusts came out of the smoke.
The locusts descended on the earth.
The locusts received power.
Their power was like the power of scorpions on the earth.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐκ τοῦ καπνοῦ ἐξῆλθον ἀκρίδες εἰς τὴν γῆν καὶ ἐδόθη αὐταῖς ἐξουσία ὡς ἔχουσιν ἐξουσίαν οἱ σκορπίοι τῆς γῆς

passages.text: They were told not to harm the grass of the earth or any plant or tree, but only those who did not have the seal of God on their foreheads.
passages.sermon:
God gave the locusts a command.
The locusts must not harm the grass of the earth.
The locusts must not harm any green plant.
The locusts must not harm any tree.
The locusts may harm only certain people.
These people do not have the seal of God on their foreheads.
passages.original: καὶ ἐρρέθη αὐταῖς ἵνα μὴ ἀδικήσουσιν τὸν χόρτον τῆς γῆς οὐδὲ πᾶν χλωρὸν οὐδὲ πᾶν δένδρον εἰ μὴ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους οἵτινες οὐκ ἔχουσι τὴν σφραγῖδα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων

passages.text: The locusts were not given power to kill them, but only to torment them for five months, and their torment was like the stinging of a scorpion.
passages.sermon:
The locusts came out of the smoke.
The locusts received power.
The locusts did not receive power to kill people.
The locusts received power to torment people.
The torment would last five months.
The torment was like the sting of a scorpion.
passages.original: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ ἀποκτείνωσιν αὐτούς ἀλλ’ ἵνα βασανισθήσονται μῆνας πέντε καὶ ὁ βασανισμὸς αὐτῶν ὡς βασανισμὸς σκορπίου ὅταν παίσῃ ἄνθρωπον

passages.text: In those days men will seek death and will not find it; they will long to die, but death will escape them.
passages.sermon:
In those days, people will look for death.
They will not find death.
People will want to die.
Death will run away from them.
passages.original: καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ζητήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι τὸν θάνατον καὶ οὐ μὴ εὑρήσουσιν αὐτόν καὶ ἐπιθυμήσουσιν ἀποθανεῖν καὶ φεύγει ὁ θάνατος ἀπ’ αὐτῶν

passages.text: And the locusts looked like horses prepared for battle, with something like crowns of gold on their heads, and faces like the faces of men.
passages.sermon:
The locusts appeared.
They looked like horses ready for battle.
They had something like crowns of gold on their heads.
Their faces looked like human faces.
passages.original: Καὶ τὰ ὁμοιώματα τῶν ἀκρίδων ὅμοια ἵπποις ἡτοιμασμένοις εἰς πόλεμον καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν ὡς στέφανοι ὅμοιοι χρυσῷ καὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὡς πρόσωπα ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: They had hair like that of women, and teeth like those of lions.
passages.sermon: The locusts appeared in the vision.\r\nThey had hair like the hair of women.\r\nTheir teeth were like the teeth of lions.
passages.original: καὶ εἶχον τρίχας ὡς τρίχας γυναικῶν καὶ οἱ ὀδόντες αὐτῶν ὡς λεόντων ἦσαν

passages.text: They also had thoraxes like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the roar of many horses and chariots rushing into battle.
passages.sermon:
The locusts had thoraxes.
Their thoraxes looked like breastplates made of iron.
Their wings made a loud sound.
The sound of their wings was like the roar of many horses.
The sound was also like chariots rushing into battle.
passages.original: καὶ εἶχον θώρακας ὡς θώρακας σιδηροῦς καὶ ἡ φωνὴ τῶν πτερύγων αὐτῶν ὡς φωνὴ ἁρμάτων ἵππων πολλῶν τρεχόντων εἰς πόλεμον

passages.text: They had tails with stingers like scorpions, which had the power to injure people for five months.
passages.sermon:
These beings had tails.
Their tails looked like scorpions’ tails.
Their tails had stingers.
Their tails gave them power.
They could injure people with their tails.
They could do this for five months.
passages.original: καὶ ἔχουσιν οὐρὰς ὁμοίας σκορπίοις καὶ κέντρα καὶ ἐν ταῖς οὐραῖς αὐτῶν ἡ ἐξουσία αὐτῶν ἀδικῆσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους μῆνας πέντε

passages.text: They were ruled by a king, the angel of the Abyss. His name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and in Greek it is Apollyon.
passages.sermon:
These beings had a king over them.
This king was the angel of the Abyss.
His name in Hebrew is Abaddon.
His name in Greek is Apollyon.
passages.original: ἔχουσιν ἐπ’ αὐτῶν βασιλέα τὸν ἄγγελον τῆς ἀβύσσου ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἑβραϊστί Ἀβαδδών καὶ ἐν τῇ Ἑλληνικῇ ὄνομα ἔχει Ἀπολλύων

passages.text: The first woe has passed. Behold, two woes are still to follow.
passages.sermon: The first woe has ended.\r\nTwo more woes will come after this.\r\n
passages.original: Ἡ Οὐαὶ ἡ μία ἀπῆλθεν ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται ἔτι δύο Οὐαὶ μετὰ ταῦτα

passages.text: Then the sixth angel sounded his trumpet, and I heard a voice from the four horns of the golden altar before God saying to the sixth angel with the trumpet, “Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates.”
passages.sermon:
The sixth angel sounded his trumpet.
I heard a voice.
The voice came from the four horns of the golden altar.
This altar stands before God.
The voice spoke to the sixth angel.
The sixth angel held the trumpet.
The voice said, “Release the four angels.”
These four angels are bound at the great river Euphrates.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ ἕκτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν μίαν ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων κεράτων τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τοῦ χρυσοῦ τοῦ ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ λέγοντα τῷ ἕκτῳ ἀγγέλῳ ὁ ἔχων τὴν σάλπιγγα Λῦσον τοὺς τέσσαρας ἀγγέλους τοὺς δεδεμένους ἐπὶ τῷ ποταμῷ τῷ μεγάλῳ Εὐφράτῃ

passages.text: So the four angels who had been prepared for this hour and day and month and year were released to kill a third of mankind.
passages.sermon:
Four angels stood ready.
God had prepared these angels for a specific time.
God chose the exact hour, day, month, and year.
Someone released the four angels at that moment.
The four angels received a task.
Their task was to kill a third of all people.
passages.original: καὶ ἐλύθησαν οἱ τέσσαρες ἄγγελοι οἱ ἡτοιμασμένοι εἰς τὴν ὥραν καὶ ἡμέραν καὶ μῆνα καὶ ἐνιαυτόν ἵνα ἀποκτείνωσιν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: And the number of mounted troops was two hundred million; I heard their number.
passages.sermon: John saw a great army of mounted troops in his vision.\r\nThe number of these mounted troops was two hundred million.\r\nJohn heard the number of the mounted troops.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν στρατευμάτων τοῦ ἱππικοῦ δισμυριάδες μυριάδων ἤκουσα τὸν ἀριθμὸν αὐτῶν

passages.text: Now the horses and riders in my vision looked like this: The riders had breastplates the colors of fire, sapphire, and sulfur. The heads of the horses were like the heads of lions, and out of their mouths proceeded fire, smoke, and sulfur.
passages.sermon:
John saw a vision.
He saw horses.
He saw riders sitting on the horses.
The riders wore breastplates.
The breastplates were the color of fire.
The breastplates were also the color of sapphire.
The breastplates were also the color of sulfur.
The horses had heads like lions.
Fire came out of the horses’ mouths.
Smoke came out of the horses’ mouths.
Sulfur came out of the horses’ mouths.
passages.original: Καὶ οὕτως εἶδον τοὺς ἵππους ἐν τῇ ὁράσει καὶ τοὺς καθημένους ἐπ’ αὐτῶν ἔχοντας θώρακας πυρίνους καὶ ὑακινθίνους καὶ θειώδεις καὶ αἱ κεφαλαὶ τῶν ἵππων ὡς κεφαλαὶ λεόντων καὶ ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν ἐκπορεύεται πῦρ καὶ καπνὸς καὶ θεῖον

passages.text: A third of mankind was killed by the three plagues of fire, smoke, and sulfur that proceeded from their mouths.
passages.sermon:
A third of all people died.
Three plagues caused their deaths.
These plagues were fire, smoke, and sulfur.
Fire, smoke, and sulfur came out of the mouths of the horses.
passages.original: ἀπὸ τῶν τριῶν πληγῶν τούτων ἀπεκτάνθησαν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐκ τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ τοῦ καπνοῦ καὶ τοῦ θείου τοῦ ἐκπορευομένου ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν

passages.text: For the power of the horses was in their mouths and in their tails; indeed, their tails were like snakes, having heads with which to inflict harm.
passages.sermon:
The horses had power in their mouths.
The horses also had power in their tails.
Their tails looked like snakes.
The tails had heads.
With these heads, the horses caused harm.
passages.original: ἡ γὰρ ἐξουσία τῶν ἵππων ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτῶν ἐστιν καὶ ἐν ταῖς οὐραῖς αὐτῶν αἱ γὰρ οὐραὶ αὐτῶν ὅμοιαι ὄφεσιν ἔχουσαι κεφαλάς καὶ ἐν αὐταῖς ἀδικοῦσιν

passages.text: Now the rest of mankind who were not killed by these plagues still did not repent of the works of their hands. They did not stop worshiping demons and idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood, which cannot see or hear or walk.
passages.sermon:
Many people survived the plagues.
These people were not killed by the plagues.
They did not repent.
They did not turn away from the works of their hands.
They continued to worship demons.
They also worshiped idols made of gold.
They worshiped idols made of silver.
They worshiped idols made of bronze.
They worshiped idols made of stone.
They worshiped idols made of wood.
These idols cannot see.
These idols cannot hear.
These idols cannot walk.
passages.original: Καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων οἳ οὐκ ἀπεκτάνθησαν ἐν ταῖς πληγαῖς ταύταις οὐδὲ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν ἵνα μὴ προσκυνήσουσιν τὰ δαιμόνια καὶ τὰ εἴδωλα τὰ χρυσᾶ καὶ τὰ ἀργυρᾶ καὶ τὰ χαλκᾶ καὶ τὰ λίθινα καὶ τὰ ξύλινα ἃ οὔτε βλέπειν δύνανται οὔτε ἀκούειν οὔτε περιπατεῖν

passages.text: Furthermore, they did not repent of their murder, sorcery, sexual immorality, and theft.
passages.sermon:
The people did not repent.
They did not turn away from their murders.
They did not stop their sorcery.
They did not leave their sexual immorality.
They did not give up their thefts.
passages.original: καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν φόνων αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῶν φαρμάκων αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῶν οὔτε ἐκ τῶν κλεμμάτων αὐτῶν
